verdict.rationale: Unreal exposes gameplay logic through Blueprint visual scripting (marketed as 'virtually the full range of concepts... available to programmers') and through C++ with full IDE debugging via Visual Studio/XCode (unreal-docs-1, unreal-docs-2/11/19/33), plus editor-only Python scripting. However, no single 'primary' scripting language fully exposes the engine API with a debugger: Blueprint has no first-class debugger for complex logic and community reports explicitly say Blueprints are 'not sufficient' for non-trivial gameplay and force a drop to C++ (unreal-comm-9, unreal-comm-12, unreal-comm-19), while C++ requires full compilation/IDE tooling rather than being a lightweight productive scripting layer. Missing for 10: evidence of a unified productive scripting language (e.g., Python/Blueprint) with a dedicated debugger that has 1:1 parity with the full gameplay API, and independent confirmation that Blueprint debugging scales to production complexity.
